sentences.text:
"1) We have heard the learned Special Officer, who has been appointed in this matter,
as well as the learned advocate appearing for the petitioner, learned senior standing counsel for the State, learned advocate for NHAI and the learned advocate for the other respondents.
2. Learned Special Officer has filed a compilation containing Minutes of meeting convened by him at the office of the District Collector, North 24 Parganas.

From the Minutes of the meeting it is seen that though the contractors of NHAI were ready to commence the work but there were objections raised by the local people preventing the work from being commenced and the grievance of the NHAI was that sufficient police were not deployed as a result the work could not be commenced.
Ultimately it was decided that the work will be commenced on 9th December, 2024.

This facts have been recorded in the Minutes of 30th November, 2024, signed by the learned Special Officer as well as the Additional District Magistrate and Competent Authority, Land Acquisition, North 24 Parganas and Additional Superintendent of Police, Barasat Police District.
In spite of having fixed 9th December, 2024, as the date for commencement of the work, the contractor could not do so.

Accordingly the Project Director, NHAI has addressed the District Magistrate, North 24 Parganas,
by letter dated 9th December, 2024, clearly stating out the difficulties faced by them and also placing on records that compensation under section 3G of the National Highways Act amounting to Rs.211.78 crores with an additional amount of Rs.488.92 crores totaling to Rs.700.70 crores have already been paid to the land losers.
It appears that the persons who are now agitating and preventing the project from being completed are the land encroachers.
District administration and police administration should deal with the matter with iron hand so that the project which is the utmost public importance is implemented.

3. The learned senior standing counsel for the State on instruction submitted that a date may be fixed by the court and the District Administration and Police Administration will ensure that the contractors of NHAI are able to commence work and in respect of a small percentage of land losers to whom the compensation has not been disbursed will be disbursed in the meantime.
4. In the light of the above, we direct that the work shall be commenced by the contractor of NHAI from 1st March, 2025.

The District Administration shall ensure deployment of officers on ground and they should carry with them necessary documents with regard to compensation which has already been disbursed and other relevant details.

The Police Administration, namely, the Additional Superintendent of Police, Barasat Police district shall ensure deployment of adequate number of police personnel at the site and ensure that the encroachers or illegal occupants on the margin of the existing roads do not object to implementation of the project.

The Project Director in his letter dated 9th December, 2024, has stated that on 9th December, 2024, the contractor was ready to commence the work and a small contingent of 5-6 police officers were deployed.
Inspector-in-Charge of Amdanga was not present at the site but he had sent a Whatsapp message to the undersigned to send the representative of NHAI, who were already present at the site.

Therefore,
the Project Director would state that on account of lack of broader presence impacted the preparedness and ability of the contractor to commence work.

The learned senior standing counsel on behalf of the State has assured the court that adequate deployment of police force will be made and in the event adequate police force is not available in the Barasat Police district, the Debesh Saha vs Union Of India & Ors on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111477617/

sentences.text: 2 Superintendent of Police, Barasat Police district or higher police officials should request adequate number of police force from the Reserve Police Force/Battalion so that the public project should not be hampered.
That apart, when compensation has already been disbursed to the land losers and having received the compensation they have no right to object to the implementation of the project.
We are informed that the objectors are the encroachers.
The respondent-State should realise the fact that the encroachers have no vested right and they should be dealt with in a proper manner so that the project is implemented seamlessly.
An action taken report be filed by the District Administration, Barasat and the Police Administration, Barasat on the next hearing date.
Learned Special Officer is at liberty to file a report as to action taken on and from 1st March, 2025 and onwards.

5. We further direct the NHAI to provide all logistical support, amenities with the travel accommodation commensurate to the status of Special Officer who is designated as senior advocate along with his junior associates so as to enable them to travel for inspection and hold meetings in respect of highways in question being renumbered as NH-12, NH-31, NH-31D, NH-31C.

Though the learned advocate for NHAI submitted that this issue was covered by the earlier order, we make it clear that the above projects should be implemented by NHAI and they should bear in mind by doing so it will be in public interest to enable the contractor of NHAI to seamlessly continue with the work entrusted to them."
Learned counsel appearing as Special Officer submits that as there is no police protection, work cannot proceed in the Amdanga region which falls under the Barasat Police District, North 24 Parganas.

State is represented by Mr. Banerjee, who is requested to take all necessary steps to comply with the directions passed in the order dated 13.02.2025 and file a report regarding the safety and security of the officers of NHAI and their contractors in the area as mentioned above.
Learned counsel appearing for the National Highways Authority of India is also requested to file a report regarding the progress of the work at Amdanga region within Barasat Police District.
Let the reports as mentioned above, be filed within 10 days from date.
Let this matter again appear in the list on 22nd of April, 2025.

(Reetobroto Kumar Mitra, J.) (Rajarshi Bharadwaj, J.)
